provider.name: Tropicos
provider.organization_type: global plant nomenclature, taxonomy, bibliography, herbarium specimen, person, project, distribution, image, API, and floristic-reference infrastructure
provider.description: Tropicos is the Missouri Botanical Garden's botanical information system. It links scientific names, accepted names, synonyms, authors, publications, specimens, type material, people, images, geographic distributions, floristic projects, and machine-readable services.
institutional_context: Missouri Botanical Garden Herbarium and Library
Global floristic, monographic, herbarium, and biodiversity-data partners
Botanists, taxonomists, collectors, curators, publishers, and software developers

purpose.summary: This file is a crawl-ready source catalog for collecting Tropicos documentation, organization, names, synonyms, classification, publications, specimens, type material, people, projects, distributions, images, API documentation, downloads, schemas, editorial workflows, data quality, licenses, citations, software, standards, and related authorities.
purpose.authoritative_notice: Tropicos, Missouri Botanical Garden, official project editors, original botanical literature, type specimens, source herbaria, official releases, and cited external authorities remain authoritative for names, publications, specimens, identifiers, rights, versions, and contacts.

notes: Verify current Tropicos Web Services base URL, version, API-key requirements, methods, parameters, formats, pagination, rate limits, and deprecations.
Verify the exact route capitalization and path conventions for Name, Reference, Specimen, Person, Project, Distribution, and Image services.
Do not infer undocumented editorial, administrative, or write endpoints from browser traffic.
Do not store API keys, passwords, cookies, tokens, or session identifiers in this manifest.
Capture exact Tropicos, Missouri Botanical Garden, project, herbarium, image, API, download, and third-party legal wording.
Separate nomenclatural facts, specimen metadata, bibliographic metadata, person data, project text, images, maps, API output, and software.
Preserve Tropicos IDs, source project, collection and institution, citation, access date, release version, license URI, rights holder, and provenance.
Do not assume specimen images, project treatments, maps, floras, or third-party literature share the same rights as factual name records.
Seed URLs are best-effort and were not live-verified in this session.
The acquisition program should update retrieval, content, review, and verification fields in place.
Tropicos routes, API methods, API-key requirements, project URLs, download formats, schemas, field names, and legal pages may change; preserve redirect and failure metadata.
Do not recursively crawl every name, reference, specimen, person, project, distribution, image, API result, or download row when the task is documentation acquisition.
Do not store API keys, credentials, passwords, cookies, tokens, private editorial notes, unpublished project data, or session identifiers.
Nomenclatural facts, specimen metadata, bibliography, person data, project content, images, maps, API output, downloads, and software may carry different rights.

Always preserve Tropicos name, reference, specimen, person, project, distribution, and image IDs; accepted-name and parent relationships; scientific name, authorship, rank, status, publication, type data, institution and catalog number, collector and collection number, dates, localities, coordinates, project and source, release and API versions, citation, rights, source URL, and provenance.
